original_requirements:
## Module: office_equipment_tracker
Track office equipment assigned to employees — who currently holds what, check-out/return dates, and condition notes.

### Models
- **office.equipment**: name (Char, required), serial_number (Char), equipment_type (Selection: laptop/phone/monitor/peripheral/other), state (Selection: available/checked_out/in_repair/retired, default=available), employee_id (Many2one hr.employee, current holder), checkout_date (Date), return_date (Date), condition_notes (Text), company_id (Many2one res.company, default current company)
  - Relations: Many2one to hr.employee (employee_id), Many2one to res.company
  - Computed fields: none (all fields stored/direct)

### Business Rules
- State flow: available -> checked_out -> available (returned), with side branches to in_repair and retired from any active state.
- Checking out: requires employee_id to be set; checkout_date auto-fills to today when state becomes checked_out; return_date is cleared.
- Returning: available action clears employee_id (current-holder-only model, no history kept) and sets return_date to today.
- Marking in_repair or retired: clears employee_id (item is no longer held by anyone) but preserves condition_notes.
- Constraint: employee_id is required whenever state = checked_out (validated on save).
- Constraint: serial_number, if provided, should be unique across active (non-retired) equipment.
- No overdue/reminder logic (not requested) and no historical log model — only the current assignment is tracked.

### Views & UX
- List view (main working view): name, serial_number, equipment_type, state, employee_id, checkout_date, return_date. Color/decoration by state (e.g. red for in_repair, muted for retired).
- Form view: header with state as a status bar (buttons to check out / return / send to repair / retire), main group with identification fields (name, serial_number, equipment_type), assignment group (employee_id, checkout_date, return_date), and condition_notes as a full-width text area.
- Search view: filters by state (Available/Checked Out/In Repair/Retired) and group-by Employee, Equipment Type, State.
- No kanban board requested — list-first workflow.
- OWL complexity: none — all standard views/widgets.
- Responsive: standard Odoo responsive list/form, no custom mobile work needed.

### Security
- Group "Equipment Administrator": full create/read/write/unlink on office.equipment; manages checkout/return/repair/retire actions.
- Group "Equipment Viewer" (implicit, all internal users): read-only access to office.equipment, restricted by record rule to records where employee_id.user_id = current user.
- Record rule: Admin group sees all records (no domain); Viewer group domain [('employee_id.user_id', '=', user.id)].
- Menu structure: top-level "Equipment" menu -> "All Equipment" (list, admin-visible) ; employees access their own items via the same list/menu filtered by the record rule (menu visible to all internal users, content auto-restricted).

### Demo Data
- office.equipment: 15 records — mix of laptops, phones, monitors, keyboards/peripherals.
  - ~8 checked_out, each assigned to a different demo employee (from hr demo data) with realistic checkout_date values spread over the last 6 months.
  - ~4 available (unassigned, no dates).
  - 2 in_repair with condition_notes describing an issue (e.g. "Screen flickering, sent to vendor for repair").
  - 1 retired with condition_notes noting end-of-life reason.

### Constraints & Notes
- No assignment history is kept per explicit decision — reassigning an item simply overwrites the current holder; if history becomes a future need, this can be added as a separate log model without breaking this structure.
- No overdue-date alerting or scheduled notifications in this scope.
- Multi-company: company_id included for data isolation since equipment is a company asset, but no multi-currency/valuation fields requested.
module_summary:
{
  "summary": "Built office_equipment_tracker, a backend Odoo 19 module tracking company office equipment and its current holder. Single model office.equipment with a state workflow (available/checked_out/in_repair/retired) driven by header buttons that auto-fill checkout/return dates and clear the holder. Conditional serial-number uniqueness across non-retired items is enforced with a friendly pre-check in create/write plus a partial unique DB index as a concurrency backstop. Security uses two groups (Equipment Administrator full CRUD, Equipment Viewer read-only) with record rules restricting viewers to their own equipment and a global multi-company isolation rule. Verified on live Odoo 19: installed, 10/10 tests pass, api_test failed_checks=0.",
  "risk_patterns": [
    "partial unique index created in _auto_init via create_index(unique=True, where=...) — DB backstop separate from Python check",
    "uniqueness validated in create/write overrides before super() rather than @api.constrains (avoids raw IntegrityError reaching the user)",
    "record rule with relational domain employee_id.user_id = user.id for viewer isolation",
    "auto-generated model external id (model_office_equipment) referenced in security XML — flagged as false positive by static semantic validator"
  ],
  "critical_flows": [
    "Create equipment, set current holder, click Check Out — state becomes checked_out and checkout_date is today",
    "Click Return on a checked-out item — holder cleared, state available, return_date is today",
    "Click Send to Repair / Retire — holder cleared but condition_notes preserved",
    "Save a checked_out record without a holder — blocked with ValidationError",
    "Create two active items with the same serial_number — blocked; reuse a retired item's serial — allowed",
    "Log in as a non-admin internal user — see only equipment whose holder maps to your user via the record rule",
    "Group the list by Employee / Equipment Type / Status and filter by each state"
  ]
}
critical_flows: Create available equipment, open form, set employee_id, click 'Check Out' button—verify state changes to checked_out, checkout_date is today, return_date is empty
Open checked_out equipment, click 'Return' button—verify state changes to available, employee_id cleared, return_date is today
Open any active equipment, click 'Send to Repair'—verify state changes to in_repair, employee_id cleared, condition_notes preserved
Open any equipment, click 'Retire'—verify state changes to retired, employee_id cleared, condition_notes preserved, equipment no longer appears in 'available' filters
Attempt to save checked_out equipment without employee_id—verify ValidationError blocks save with user-friendly message

Create two active equipment with identical serial_number—verify second create fails with uniqueness constraint error; create retired equipment, then create new active with same serial_number—verify allowed

Log in as Equipment Viewer (internal user), create equipment assigned to you—verify you see it in list; click Return to clear holder—verify record disappears from your list view (record rule now excludes it)
Log in as Equipment Administrator—verify all equipment visible regardless of employee_id or company_id; verify full CRUD permissions (create, edit, delete) work

Open list view with 8 checked_out items, group by Employee—verify items group under assigned employees, group by State—verify items group correctly under checked_out/available/in_repair/retired buckets

Test multi-company isolation: create equipment in Company A, switch user context to Company B—verify Company B admin sees only Company B equipment, equipment from Company A is filtered out by record rule
Navigate from list to form via row click on various states—verify appropriate action buttons are visible/hidden (Check Out button on available only, Return/Repair/Retire on non-available)
Verify checkout_date does not change on subsequent writes to a checked_out record if state remains checked_out—test that date-filling logic only triggers on state transition, not every save
risk_patterns: State workflow side-effects in create/write overrides auto-fill checkout_date and return_date; if user saves a checked_out record twice, dates may unexpectedly update—needs guards to only fill dates on state transition, not every write

Conditional uniqueness on serial_number enforced by both Python pre-check and partial unique DB index (where state != 'retired'); Python check may not catch race conditions under concurrent writes—verify DB index WHERE clause syntax is valid for Odoo 19 CREATE INDEX

Record rule for Equipment Viewer restricts visibility to [('employee_id.user_id', '=', user.id)]; after returning equipment, employee_id is cleared and viewer loses visibility—non-admin users cannot see their own equipment history, may confuse workflow

Many2one domain employee_id.user_id in record rule assumes all hr.employee records have user_id; if employee has no user_id or user_id is deleted, record rule evaluation may fail or raise error—test with orphaned employee_id

Employee_id field required when state=checked_out enforced in create/write; if ValidationError is raised before super(), side-effects may not rollback properly—verify create/write override error handling doesn't break transaction

Search view group-by Employee will create a 'False' group for unassigned equipment (available/in_repair/retired); UI may display confusing empty or null-labeled group—consider readability on list with many unassigned items

Partial unique index only applies to non-retired records; if record is created as retired, then state changed to available, then changed to checked_out with existing serial_number, unique constraint may not trigger on second transition—verify index is checked on every state change

Action buttons (action_check_out, action_return, action_send_to_repair, action_retire) must be wired with correct states attribute to hide/show appropriately; if button is available in wrong state, workflow can become inconsistent or stuck

Company_id multi-company record rule (equipment_rule_company) must exist to isolate equipment by company; if rule is missing or permissive, users in one company may see equipment from another—verify rule domain is [('company_id', '=', user.company_id.id)]

Return_date auto-filled on state transition to available; if Equipment Viewer marks own equipment as returned (clears employee_id), they lose visibility immediately and cannot confirm return_date was recorded—test viewer perspective end-to-end
